title: Bill Belichick
wiki_lead:
William Stephen Belichick (  BEL-itch-ik, -⁠ek; born April 16, 1952) is an American football coach who is the head coach for the North Carolina Tar Heels. Regarded as one of the greatest head coaches ever, he holds numerous coaching records, including the record of most Super Bowl wins (six) as a head coach, all with the New England Patriots, along with two more during his time as the defensive coordinator of the New York Giants, for a record eight total Super Bowl victories as coach and coordinator. A renowned American football historian, Belichick is often referred to as a "student of the game" with a deep knowledge of the intricacies of each player position. During his tenure with the Patriots, Belichick was a central figure as the head coach and de facto general manager during the team's dynasty from 2001 to 2019.
Belichick is a descendant of Bill Parcells's coaching tree. He began his coaching career in 1975 as an assistant for the Baltimore Colts and became the defensive coordinator for New York Giants head coach Parcells by 1985. Parcells and Belichick won two Super Bowls together before Belichick left to become the head coach of the Cleveland Browns in 1991. He remained in Cleveland for five seasons but was fired following the team's 1995 season. Belichick rejoined Parcells, first in New England, where the team lost Super Bowl XXXI, and later with the New York Jets. After being named head coach of the Jets, Belichick resigned after only one day on the job to accept the head coaching job for the Patriots on January 27, 2000. In 24 seasons under Belichick, the Patriots won 17 AFC East division titles, made 13 appearances in the AFC Championship Game, and appeared in nine Super Bowls, with a record six wins. Overall, Belichick has won eight Super Bowl titles (the most of any individual in NFL history) and finished as runner-up four times from his combined time as an assistant and head coach.
At the time Belichick left the Patriots, he was the NFL's longest-tenured active head coach. Belichick has the most playoff coaching wins all-time with 31 and ranks third in regular-season coaching wins in the NFL with 302. He is also in second place for combined regular-season and postseason wins, and also second place for most regular-season coaching wins with one franchise. Belichick is one of only three head coaches who have won six NFL titles. He was named the AP NFL Coach of the Year for the 2003, 2007, and 2010 seasons. Belichick has also been selected to the NFL 2000s All-Decade Team, NFL 2010s All-Decade Team, and the NFL 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

Early life and education
Belichick was born in Nashville, Tennessee, on April 16, 1952, the son of Jeannette (née Munn) and Steve Belichick. Belichick was named after College Football Hall of Fame coach Bill Edwards, who was his godfather. grok_lead: Bill Belichick (born April 16, 1952) is an American football coach recognized for his strategic acumen and record-setting success in the National Football League (NFL), particularly during his tenure as head coach of the New England Patriots from 2000 to 2023, where he secured six Super Bowl victoriesâthe most by any head coach in league historyâand currently leads the University of North Carolina Tar Heels football program. Born in Nashville, Tennessee, to Steve Belichick, a longtime college and professional coach, Belichick entered the profession in 1975 as a special teams assistant with the Baltimore Colts, progressing through roles with the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, and New York Giants, where as defensive coordinator he contributed to two Super Bowl wins under Bill Parcells. Belichick's Patriots era, often termed a dynasty, featured 17 division titles, nine AFC championships, and 35 playoff victories, achieved through adaptive schemes emphasizing player versatility, situational awareness, and a "do your job" ethos that prioritized execution over talent disparities. His partnership with quarterback Tom Brady yielded five of those Super Bowls, with the duo's 219 regular-season wins and 35 playoff triumphs setting benchmarks for sustained excellence amid high expectations and roster turnover. However, Belichick's career includes notable controversies, such as the 2007 Spygate incident, in which the Patriots videotaped New York Jets defensive signals from an unauthorized sideline position, resulting in a $500,000 fine for Belichick, a $250,000 team penalty, and forfeiture of a first-round draft pick after league investigation confirmed a violation of rules against such filming. The 2015 Deflategate scandal further scrutinized the team when footballs used by Brady were found underinflated, prompting NFL penalties including Brady's four-game suspension (later reduced), though Belichick maintained the practices stemmed from equipment handling rather than intentional deception. In December 2024, Belichick transitioned to college football as UNC's head coach, inheriting a program amid roster flux and administrative challenges, with early 2025 results reflecting adaptation struggles but underscoring his reputation for defensive innovation and long-term program-building. His overall NFL coaching record stands at 333 wins against 178 losses, including playoffs, affirming his status as one of the game's most influential tacticians despite criticisms of win-at-all-costs approaches.
